statements.label: opt2
statements.text: Number of years of schooling is not counted in the HDI.
statements.fact_source: UNDP Human Development Report, Technical Notes (2016)
statements.true_fact: Years of schooling are the education dimension.

statements.label: opt3
statements.text: Ownership of basic assets is not counted in the HDI.
statements.fact_source: UNDP Human Development Report, Technical Notes (2016)

statements.label: opt4
statements.text: Life expectancy at birth is not counted in the HDI.
statements.fact_source: UNDP Human Development Report, Technical Notes (2016)

reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: HDI = health + education + income; MPI adds assets, cooking fuel, sanitation etc.

leaf_note: No statistics leaf in the G2 syllabus; nearest quantitative leaf is national-income measurement.
micro_topic: Statistics > dispersion > standard deviation

sqrt of variance, in original units

reconstruction.correct_statement: Standard deviation = square root of variance.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Variance = SD^2; coefficient of variation = SD/mean x 100.

leaf_note: Innovation theory; nearest leaf is STI policy (no extension/communication leaf).
micro_topic: Innovation > Rogers' diffusion of innovations > adopter categories
core_fact: E.M. Rogers (1962) classified adopters in order of adoption: innovators (2.5%), early adopters (13.5%), early majority (34%), late majority (34%), laggards (16%).

statements.fact_source: E.M. Rogers, Diffusion of Innovations (1962)

statements.label: step3-4
statements.text: Early Majority adopt before Late Majority.
statements.fact_source: E.M. Rogers, Diffusion of Innovations (1962)

statements.label: step4-5
statements.text: Late Majority adopt before Laggards.
statements.fact_source: E.M. Rogers, Diffusion of Innovations (1962)

reconstruction.correct_statement: Adopters: innovators -> early adopters -> early majority -> late majority -> laggards.
reconstruction.decisive: Innovators, Early Adopters, Early Majority, Late Majority, Laggards
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Rogers' sequence: I-EA-EM-LM-L (2.5/13.5/34/34/16).

leaf_note: Defamation is a reasonable restriction on Art. 19(1)(a); no media-law leaf exists.

reconstruction.correct_statement: Innuendo is a form of defamation (keyed as slander).
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Defamation: libel (permanent form) vs slander (spoken); innuendo = hidden meaning.

key_note: Innuendo is strictly an implied defamatory meaning, not only spoken; APPSC's key 'Slander' kept.

leaf_note: Press freedom is part of Art. 19(1)(a) Fundamental Rights; no media leaf.
micro_topic: Freedom of speech > freedom of press > democracy; new media
core_fact: Freedom of the press (implicit in Art. 19(1)(a), Romesh Thappar 1950) is essential to democracy; new media enable participatory communication - both true, but the second does not explain the first.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A free press is necessary for a vibrant democracy.
statements.fact_source: Romesh Thappar v State of Madras (1950); Indian Express Newspapers (1985)

statements.label: R
statements.text: New media technologies have facilitated participatory communication.
statements.fact_source: Standard mass-communication texts

statements.text: New media's participatory communication is the reason a free press is necessary for democracy.

phrases.would_be_correct_if: R stated the democratic watchdog role of the press

reconstruction.why: B concerns technology; A concerns democratic theory.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: In A-R, test the link separately: true + true does not mean 'explains'.
